p.src: Now, when Old Master Song set a ladder against the wall and climbed up to look, he saw more than a hundred men amid a forest of torches. At their head were two newly appointed constables of Yuncheng County, a pair of brothers: one named Zhao Neng and the other Zhao De.

u.src: Now, when Old Master Song set a ladder against the wall and climbed up to look, he saw more than a hundred men amid a forest of torches. At their head were two newly appointed constables of Yuncheng County, a pair of brothers: one named Zhao Neng and the other Zhao De.

p.src: The two called out, “Old Master Song, if you know what is good for you, hand over your son Song Jiang, and we shall treat him with consideration. But if you refuse to let him answer to the authorities, we shall seize you, his old father, along with him.” Old Master Song said, “When did Song Jiang ever return?” Zhao Neng said, “Enough of your nonsense! Someone saw him drinking at Village Head Zhang’s tavern by the village entrance and then returning, and others followed him all the way here. How can you possibly deny it?” Beside the ladder, Song Jiang said, “Father, why waste words arguing with them? It will do no harm for me to step forward and answer to the authorities. I have acquaintances in both the county and prefectural offices, and since the offense has already been covered by an amnesty, my sentence will surely be reduced. Why plead with these scoundrels? That Zhao fellow is a crafty rogue who has suddenly risen to be a constable. What does he know of justice or principle? He has no friendship with me either, so it would be useless to beg him.” Old Master Song wept. “It is I who have brought this suffering upon you, my son.” Song Jiang said, “Do not grieve, Father. Being brought before the authorities may actually prove fortunate. If instead I hide among the rivers and lakes and fall in with a band of brothers who kill and burn, I shall be caught in their net. How then could I ever see you again? Even if I am sentenced to exile in some distant prefecture, the term will have a limit. When I return one day, I shall still be able to attend you morning and evening for the rest of your life.” Old Master Song said, “Since you put it that way, my son, I shall spend what is needed among high and low to secure you a favorable place of exile.”

p.src: Song Jiang climbed the ladder and called out, “Stop making such a commotion. My offense has now been pardoned, so I certainly shall not be put to death. Please, both constables, come into my humble manor and share a few cups with us. Tomorrow we shall go together before the magistrate.” Zhao Neng said, “Do not try any tricks to lure us inside.” Song Jiang said, “How could I bring trouble upon my father and brother? Come straight into the house without concern.”

p.src: Song Jiang came down the ladder, opened the manor gate, and invited the two constables to sit in the main hall. Though it was already night, chickens and geese were slaughtered and a feast of wine was laid before them. The hundred local soldiers and their companions were all supplied with food and wine and given gifts of money and goods. They took twenty taels of fine silver and presented it to the two constables as “money for appearances.” Indeed:

p.src: Show constables money and their manner turns fair; without it, they glare at you foully. Thus money is called “good for appearances”; money alone knows neither law nor magistrate.

p.src: That night, the two constables lodged at Song Jiang’s manor. At the fifth watch the next morning, they went together to wait before the county offices. When they escorted him into the county offices at daybreak, the magistrate had just entered the court and taken his seat. Seeing the constables Zhao Neng and Zhao De escort Song Jiang to answer to the authorities, Magistrate Shi Wenbin was delighted and ordered Song Jiang to submit a confession. u.src: That night, the two constables lodged at Song Jiang’s manor.
At the fifth watch the next morning, they went together to wait before the county offices.
When they escorted him into the county offices at daybreak, the magistrate had just entered the court and taken his seat.
Seeing the constables Zhao Neng and Zhao De escort Song Jiang to answer to the authorities, Magistrate Shi Wenbin was delighted and ordered Song Jiang to submit a confession.
Song Jiang immediately wrote out his confession in one hand:

p.src: “In the autumn of the year before last, I improperly contracted to maintain Yan Poxi as my concubine. Because she proved ill-behaved, we quarreled and fought while I was under the influence of wine, resulting in her accidental death, after which I remained a fugitive to evade punishment. Now that I have been apprehended and brought before the authorities, the former circumstances have been investigated. I freely confess the foregoing, accept my guilt, and have nothing to plead in my defense.”

u.src: “In the autumn of the year before last, I improperly contracted to maintain Yan Poxi as my concubine. Because she proved ill-behaved, we quarreled and fought while I was under the influence of wine, resulting in her accidental death, after which I remained a fugitive to evade punishment.

Now that I have been apprehended and brought before the authorities, the former circumstances have been investigated. I freely confess the foregoing, accept my guilt, and have nothing to plead in my defense.”

p.src: After reading it, the magistrate ordered Song Jiang confined in jail to await judgment. When the people throughout the county heard that Song Jiang had been captured, there was not one who did not cherish him. They all went to the magistrate to plead for mercy on his behalf, recounting all the good he had done in ordinary times. The magistrate himself was already largely inclined to deal leniently with him. He therefore accepted the confession as submitted, exempted Song Jiang from the long cangue and hand-fetters, and allowed him to remain loosely confined within the jail. Old Master Song personally bribed officials high and low, spending money and silk. By then, Old Yan had herself been dead for half a year, so there was no aggrieved complainant. As for Zhang San, now that he had lost his whore, he had no reason to come and pursue the grievance. The county offices compiled the case documents and, when the sixty-day period expired, closed the case and transferred Song Jiang to Jizhou for judgment. The prefect examined the grounds for the transfer. Since the matter fell under an amnesty issued after the offense, the sentence had already been reduced. Song Jiang was given twenty strokes on the back and tattooed and exiled to the prison settlement at Jiangzhou. Some of the prefectural officials also knew Song Jiang, and he had money to spend besides. The punishment was what they called “nominal flogging and tattooed exile”; with no complainant to press evidence and everyone interceding for him, it was not carried out with any great severity. In the hall they placed a traveling cangue upon him, issued an official writ, and assigned two escort officers, none other than Zhang Qian and Li Wan.

p.src: The two officers received the documents and escorted Song Jiang to the front of the prefectural offices. Song Jiang’s father, Old Master Song, and his brother Song Qing were waiting there. They set out wine for the two officers and provided them with some silver for the journey. They had Song Jiang change his clothes, tied up his bundle, and put hemp sandals on his feet. Old Master Song called Song Jiang aside to a secluded spot and admonished him: “I know Jiangzhou to be a good region, a land rich in fish and rice. I spent money expressly to have you sent there. Be patient and keep your heart at ease. I shall send Fourth Brother to visit you, and whenever a trustworthy traveler is available, I shall regularly send money for your expenses. Your road now takes you directly past Liangshan Marsh. If those men should come down from the mountain, seize you, and ask you to join their band, you must under no circumstances follow them and let people revile you as disloyal and unfilial. Remember this above all else. Take your time on the road, my son. If Heaven has pity, you will return soon, so that father and son may be reunited and the brothers gathered together once more.” Shedding tears, Song Jiang bowed farewell to his father, while his brother Song Qing accompanied him for part of the road. As they parted, Song Jiang instructed his brother: “Do not worry about me after I leave. My only concern is that Father is advanced in years, while I, repeatedly entangled in legal troubles, must now leave my home and native place. Brother, remain at home and attend him morning and evening. Do not come to Jiangzhou on my account, abandoning Father with no one to care for him. I have many acquaintances throughout the rivers and lakes. Whomever I meet will surely help me, so I shall have means enough to cover my expenses. If Heaven takes pity, one day I shall return!” Song Qing shed tears, bowed farewell, and returned home to attend his father, Old Master Song. Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: To speak only of Song Jiang setting out with the two officers: Zhang Qian and Li Wan had received silver from him, and they also respected him as a gallant man, so throughout the journey they did nothing but attend to his needs. The three traveled for a day and lodged at an inn that evening. They lit a fire and cooked some rice, then bought wine and meat to entertain the two officers. Song Jiang said to them, “To tell you both the truth, our present road passes directly by Liangshan Marsh. There are several gallant men in the mountain stronghold who know my name. I fear they may come down the mountain to seize me and needlessly give you a fright. Tomorrow, let the three of us rise early and take only the lesser paths. It will do no harm to walk a few extra li.” The two officers said, “Clerk, if you had not told us, how could we have known? We know the lesser paths ourselves. If we go that way, we certainly shall not run into them.”

p.src: That night, they settled their plans. The next day they rose at the fifth watch, made a fire, and prepared a meal. The two constables and Song Jiang left the inn and traveled only by minor paths. After they had gone some thirty li, a band of men suddenly came around the far side of a slope ahead. At the sight of them, Song Jiang inwardly cried out in dismay. The newcomer was none other than the valiant Red-Haired Demon, Liu Tang, leading thirty or fifty men straight at the two constables to kill them. Zhang Qian and Li Wan huddled together in terror and dropped to their knees. Song Jiang called out, “Brother, whom do you mean to kill?” Liu Tang replied, “Brother, if we do not kill these two wretches, what are we waiting for?” Song Jiang said, “Do not stain your hands. Give me the sword and I will kill them myself.” The two men could only lament, “This time we are truly done for.” Liu Tang handed the sword to Song Jiang. A poem says:

p.src: Guilty before the law, he yet refused to flee; rescued at every turn, his resolve grew firmer still. From a generous heart arose a clever plan: he spared the constables, yet borrowed a sword.

p.src: Taking the sword, Song Jiang asked Liu Tang, “Why do you wish to kill the constables?” Liu Tang said, “By command of our elder brothers on the mountain, men were sent to inquire into your case. We were about to storm the jail at Yuncheng County, but then learned that you had never been imprisoned and had suffered no hardship. Now we have learned that you have been sentenced to exile in Jiangzhou. Fearing we might miss you on the road, the chiefs ordered parties to wait in all four directions, welcome you, and invite you up the mountain. How can we leave these two constables alive?” Song Jiang said, “This is not your brotherly kindness raising Song Jiang up; it would instead condemn me as disloyal and unfilial. If you mean to coerce me in this fashion, you are merely driving Song Jiang to his death. I would rather die now.” He raised the sword to his throat to cut it. Liu Tang hurriedly seized his arm and said, “Brother, wait. Let us discuss this calmly.” With that, he wrested the sword from Song Jiang’s hand. Song Jiang said, “If you brothers truly take pity on Song Jiang, allow me to go to the prison settlement at Jiangzhou and serve out my term. When I return, I will meet with you then.” Liu Tang said, “Brother, I dare not decide this matter myself. On the main road ahead, our strategist, Scholar Wu, and Commandant Hua are waiting expressly to welcome you. Allow me to send a man to invite them here so that we may consult together.” Song Jiang said, “This is my sole answer, however you may discuss it among yourselves.”

p.src: Not long after a young bandit had gone to report, Wu Yong and Hua Rong appeared, riding ahead with several dozen horsemen behind them, and came galloping up. After they dismounted and exchanged greetings, Hua Rong immediately said, “Why have you not removed our elder brother’s cangue?” Song Jiang said, “Worthy brother, what are you saying? This is the law of the realm. How could anyone dare tamper with it without authority?” Scholar Wu laughed and said, “I understand our elder brother’s meaning. That is easily arranged: we simply need not keep you in the stronghold. Chief Chao has not seen you for a long time, and now wishes to speak a few heartfelt words with you. We ask only that you visit the stronghold and talk with us briefly; then we will send you on your way.” Hearing this, Song Jiang said, “Only you, sir, truly understand my mind.” They helped the two constables to their feet, and Song Jiang said, “Set their minds at ease. I would rather die myself than let them come to harm.” The two constables said, “Our lives depend entirely upon your protection, Clerk Song.”

p.src: The whole party left the main road and came to a reedy bank, where boats were already waiting. They were ferried across to the main road before the mountain, then had Song Jiang carried in a mountain sedan chair until they reached the Broken Gold Pavilion, where they rested. The young bandits were sent in every direction to summon all the chiefs. They gathered to welcome Song Jiang up the mountain and met him in the Hall of Righteous Assembly. Chao Gai said, “Ever since you saved our lives at Yuncheng and we brothers came here, not a day has passed without our remembering your great kindness. Recently, moreover, you introduced so many heroes to our mountain, bringing glory to this humble stronghold. We have no way to repay such favors.” Song Jiang replied, “Since we parted, this humble man killed an adulterous woman and fled into the wide world, where I wandered for a year and a half. I had intended to come up the mountain to visit you, brother, but happened to meet Shi Yong at a village inn. He brought a letter from home saying only that my father had passed away. But it turned out that my father, fearing I would join the heroes here, had written the letter falsely to call me home. Though I openly faced prosecution, thanks to the consideration shown by those above and below, I suffered no grave injury. Now I have been exiled to Jiangzhou, which is not a bad place either. Having just received your summons, I dared not fail to come. Now that I have seen your honored face, however, the deadline presses me. I dare not remain long and must take my leave at once.” Chao Gai said, “Why such haste? Please sit with us a little longer.” The two sat in the central seats. Song Jiang had the constables sit directly behind his chair, never allowing them to leave him by so much as a step.

p.src: Chao Gai summoned the many chiefs to pay their respects to Song Jiang. They then sat in two rows while the lesser leaders poured wine. Chao Gai first offered him a cup. Then came the strategist, Scholar Wu, followed by Gongsun Sheng and all the others down to Bai Sheng, each offering him wine in turn. After several rounds of wine, Song Jiang rose and thanked them, saying, “This amply shows the affection you brothers bear me. But Song Jiang is a convicted prisoner and dares not linger. I must take my leave now.” Chao Gai said, “Brother, why treat us with such distance? Since you will not allow us to harm the two constables, we can give them plenty of gold and silver and send them back. They need only say that you were seized by us at Liangshan Marsh, and no one could blame them.” Song Jiang said, “Brother, speak no more of this. That would not be honoring Song Jiang; it would plainly be bringing misery upon me. My aged father is still at home, yet Song Jiang has never served him with filial devotion for even a single day. How could I dare disobey his teachings and bring trouble upon him? Previously, carried away by impulse, I set out to join you all. By Heaven’s good fortune, Shi Yong happened to meet me at a village inn and directed me home. My father explained the reason for his ruse and said he would rather have this humble man openly face the law and swiftly be sentenced to exile. He admonished me again and again. As I departed, he charged me a thousand times over not to pursue my own pleasure and thereby bring suffering upon the household, lest my aged father be burdened with grief, alarm, and fear. Thus my father expressly instructed Song Jiang. If this humble man were heedlessly to follow you, I would rebel against Heaven’s principles above and defy my father’s teaching below, becoming a man both disloyal and unfilial. What use would there be in remaining alive? If you refuse to let Song Jiang descend the mountain, I would rather beg death at your hands.” When he had finished, tears poured down like rain, and he bowed to the ground. Chao Gai, Wu Yong, and Gongsun Sheng all helped him to his feet. Everyone said, “Since our brother is firmly resolved to go to Jiangzhou, please set your mind at ease and stay with us today. We will escort you down the mountain early tomorrow.” After urging him again and again, they prevailed upon Song Jiang to remain in the stronghold and drink with them for the day. Even when they told him to remove his cangue, he refused, and stayed beside the two constables whether sitting or rising.

Even when they told him to remove his cangue, he refused, and stayed beside the two constables whether sitting or rising.

p.src: They stayed the night, and when morning came, Song Jiang rose early, firmly resolved to leave. Scholar Wu said, “Brother, hear me out. I, Wu Yong, have a very dear friend who now serves in Jiangzhou as the chief jailer of the two courts. His surname is Dai and his given name is Zong; the people there call him Warden Dai. Because he possesses magical arts and can travel eight hundred li in a day, everyone calls him the ‘Magic Traveler.’ He is exceedingly chivalrous and generous with his wealth. Last night I wrote a letter for you to take with you, so that when you arrive you may make his acquaintance. If anything should happen, have word sent to all us brothers.” Unable to persuade him to stay, the chieftains prepared a farewell banquet and brought out a tray of gold and silver to give Song Jiang; they also gave twenty taels of silver to the two constables. They packed Song Jiang’s bundle for him, escorted him down the mountain, and one after another bade him farewell. Scholar Wu and Hua Rong escorted him across the ferry and another twenty li along the main road. Then the chieftains returned up the mountain.

p.src: Now Song Jiang set out for Jiangzhou with the two constables escorting him. The constables had seen the many men and horses in the stronghold, how every chieftain paid homage to Song Jiang, and had themselves received a good sum of silver there; so throughout the journey they waited upon him with the utmost care. After the three had traveled for more than half a month, they came to a place where a lofty ridge rose ahead. The two constables said, “Good! Once we cross this Jieyang Ridge, we will reach the Xunyang River. From there it is a short journey by water to Jiangzhou.” Song Jiang said, “The weather is warm. Let us cross the ridge while it is still early and find lodging for the night.” The constables said, “You are right, Clerk Song.” The three hurried on toward the ridge. After traveling half the day, they struggled over the crest and presently saw an inn at the foot of the ridge, backed against a sheer cliff and facing strange trees, with thatched buildings before and behind. From beneath the shade of the trees, a wine banner jutted out. Song Jiang was delighted at the sight and said to the constables, “Our bellies are parched with hunger and thirst! Since there is an inn here on the ridge, let us buy a bowl of wine before going on.” The three entered the inn. The two constables set down their baggage and leaned their staves against the wall. Song Jiang invited the two constables to sit in the seats of honor, while he took the lower seat. For half an hour no one appeared. Song Jiang called, “Why is there no proprietor here?” From within came the answer, “Coming! Coming!” A burly man emerged from a side room. This was his appearance:

p.src: His red, curling beard spread wildly; his tiger eyes, threaded with crimson, bulged round. A murderous fiend upon Jieyang Ridge, the life-claiming judge of Fengdu.

p.src: The man came out wearing a tattered headcloth and a cloth vest that left both arms bare, with a cloth towel wrapped around his waist. He saluted Song Jiang and his two companions and asked, “Travelers, how much wine would you like?” Song Jiang said, “We are hungry from walking. What meat do you have for sale?” The man replied, “Only cooked beef and unstrained white wine.” Song Jiang said, “Excellent. First cut us two catties of cooked beef and bring a quarter-measure of wine.” The man said, “Travelers, do not take offense, but at this inn on the ridge we serve wine only after the money has first been paid.” Song Jiang said, “I prefer paying before drinking myself. Let me get the silver for you now.” Song Jiang opened his bundle and took out some pieces of silver. Standing beside him, the man stole a sidelong glance. Seeing how heavy the bundle was and how rich the pickings promised to be, he was already eight parts delighted. After taking Song Jiang’s silver, he went inside, ladled out a bucket of wine, sliced a platter of beef, brought out three large bowls and three pairs of chopsticks, and began pouring the wine. As the three ate, they talked among themselves: “There are villains aplenty on the roads these days, and many thousands of brave men have fallen into their traps. They put knockout drugs in the wine and meat, stupefy their victims, rob them of their goods, and use their flesh as filling for buns. I simply do not believe such a thing could happen!” The wine seller laughed and said, “Since you three have said so, you had better not eat. Both my wine and my meat are drugged.” Song Jiang laughed. “This good fellow heard us talking about drugs and is teasing us.” The two constables said, “Good fellow, it would be nice to drink a bowl warmed.” The man said, “If you want it warm, I will take it and heat it for you.” The man heated the wine, brought it back, and poured three bowls. They were hungry and thirsty, and with wine and meat at their lips, how could they refrain from eating and drinking? Each of the three drank a bowl. At once the two constables’ eyes bulged and spittle ran from the corners of their mouths. Clutching and tugging at each other, they toppled backward. Song Jiang sprang up and cried, “How can the two of you be so drunk after only one bowl?” He stepped forward to help them, but suddenly his own head spun and his vision blurred. He fell flat to the ground, eyes wide open. The three could only stare at one another, numb and unable to move. The man in the inn said, “What a blessing! I have had no business for days, and today Heaven has sent me these three fine carcasses.” First he dragged Song Jiang backward into the human butchery by the rocky cliff and laid him on the flaying bench; then he came back and dragged the two constables inside as well. The man returned once more and carried all their bundles and baggage into the rear room. When he opened them and saw that they were filled with gold and silver, he said to himself, “I have kept this inn for many years, but never have I met a prisoner like this. How could a condemned man like him possess so much wealth? Surely it has fallen from Heaven as a gift to me!” After inspecting the bundle, the man wrapped it up again, then went to the front of the inn to wait for his helpers to return and butcher the captives.

p.src: He stood before the door watching for a while, but not a single man or woman returned. He saw only three men running up the ridge from below. He recognized them and hurried forward to greet them, saying, “Elder brother, where have you been?” One of the three, a burly fellow, replied, “We came up the ridge especially to meet someone. By my reckoning, the day he should arrive is already upon us. I have gone out every day and waited below the ridge, but he has not appeared. I truly cannot imagine where he has been delayed.” The man asked, “Who are you waiting for, elder brother?” The burly fellow said, “A truly exceptional hero.” The man asked, “What exceptional hero is that?” The burly fellow answered, “You too must have heard his great name: Song Jiang, Clerk Song of Yuncheng County in Jizhou.” The man said, “Can he be Song Gongming, the ‘Timely Rain’ of Shandong, of whom everyone in the rivers and lakes speaks?” The burly fellow said, “The very man.” The man asked again, “But why should he pass this way?” The burly fellow said, “I did not know at first. Recently, an acquaintance came from Jizhou and told me, ‘For some unknown offense, Song Jiang, Clerk Song of Yuncheng County, was charged before the prefecture of Jizhou and sentenced to penal servitude at the prison colony in Jiangzhou.’ I reckoned that he would surely come this way, since there is no other road. Even when he was still in Yuncheng County, I wanted to go and meet him. Now that he is passing this very way, how could I fail to make his acquaintance? So I have waited below the ridge day after day. I have been expecting him for four or five days, yet not a single prisoner has passed. Today I strolled up the ridge with these two brothers to buy a bowl of wine here and look in on you as well. How has business been at your tavern lately?” The man said, “I will not hide it from you, elder brother: business has been wretched these past few months. But today, thank heaven and earth, I caught three traveling wares, and they had a few possessions besides.” The burly fellow hastily asked, “What sort of men are the three?” The man said, “Two constables and one convicted man.” The fellow exclaimed in alarm, “Is the prisoner a short, dark, stout man?” The man replied, “Indeed, he is not very tall, and his face is a dark purplish brown.” The burly fellow asked urgently, “You have not laid hands on them yet, have you?” The man answered, “We only just dragged them into the cutting room. The other hands have not returned, so we have not stripped and butchered them.” The burly fellow said, “Let me see whether I recognize him.”

p.src: The four men immediately entered the human-flesh cutting room beside the rocky cliff. There, stretched upon the flaying bench, lay Song Jiang and the two constables, their heads hanging down toward the floor. The burly fellow looked at Song Jiang but did not recognize him; he examined the branded characters on his face, but could not make them out and was at a loss what to do. Suddenly a thought struck him, and he said, “Bring me the constables’ bundle. I shall know once I see their official papers.” The man said, “That is right.” He went into the room, fetched the constables’ bundle, and opened it. Inside was a large ingot of silver together with a quantity of loose silver. He untied the document pouch and read the warrant of assignment, whereupon everyone cried, “What a narrow escape!” The burly fellow said, “Heaven itself sent me up the ridge today. Thank goodness you had not yet laid hands on them—you very nearly cost my elder brother his life.” Indeed:

p.src: The burly fellow called to the man, “Quickly, fetch the antidote and revive my elder brother first.” The man too was alarmed. He hurriedly prepared the antidote and went with the burly fellow into the cutting room. They first removed the cangue, helped Song Jiang upright, and poured the antidote down his throat. The four men carried Song Jiang into the guest room at the front. Supported by the burly fellow, he gradually regained consciousness and opened his eyes wide. He looked at the men standing before him but recognized none of them. Then the burly fellow had his two brothers support Song Jiang while he bowed to the floor before him. Song Jiang asked, “Who are you? Am I not dreaming?” The wine seller also bowed before him. Returning their courtesy, Song Jiang said, “Please rise, my two good brothers. Where exactly is this place? And may I ask your honorable names?” The burly fellow said, “My surname is Li and my given name is Jun. My ancestral home is Luzhou. I earn my living as a boatman on the Yangzi River, and because I am skilled in the ways of the water, everyone calls me Li Jun, the ‘River-Mingling Dragon.’ This wine seller is a native of Jieyang Ridge. He makes his way by illicit trade, and everyone calls him Li Li, the ‘Life-Taking Judge.’ These two brothers are from the banks of the Xunyang River hereabouts. They bring illicit salt here to sell and have taken refuge in my household. Both can dive beneath the great river and handle a boat. One is called Tong Wei, the ‘Cave-Leaving Jiao Dragon,’ and the other Tong Meng, the ‘River-Churning Mirage Dragon.’” The two brothers likewise bowed four times to Song Jiang. Song Jiang asked, “You had only just drugged me unconscious. How did you come to know my name?” Li Jun said, “An acquaintance of mine recently returned from trading in Jizhou. He spoke of your great name and said that, because of some affair, you had been sent to the prison colony at Jiangzhou. For a long time I had yearned to visit your honored county and pay my respects to you, but our affinity was too slight and I never managed to go. When I heard that you were coming to Jiangzhou, I knew you must pass this way. I waited below the ridge to receive you for five or seven days running, but you did not appear. Today, with no such purpose in mind, heaven favored me by sending me up the ridge with these two brothers to buy a cup of wine. We met Li Li, and the matter came up in conversation. I was greatly alarmed and hurried to look inside the cutting room, but I did not recognize you. Then the thought suddenly came to me to fetch the official papers and inspect them, and only then did I know it was you. May I venture to ask: I heard that you served as a clerk in Yuncheng County, but for what offense have you been exiled to Jiangzhou?” Song Jiang related the whole story in detail: how he had killed Yan Poxi, how a letter had been entrusted to him at Shi Yong’s village tavern, how the affair was exposed after he returned home, and how he was now being exiled to Jiangzhou. The four men sighed and marveled without end. Li Li said, “Elder brother, why not remain here with us? Do not go to the prison colony in Jiangzhou to suffer.” Song Jiang answered, “The heroes of Liangshan Marsh begged me earnestly to stay, yet even there I refused, for fear of bringing trouble upon my aged father at home. How, then, could I remain here?” Li Jun said, “My elder brother is a righteous man and would never act recklessly. Quickly revive those two constables.” Li Li hurriedly called for his hands, who had all returned by then. They carried the constables into the guest room at the front, poured the antidote down their throats, and revived them. The two looked at one another and said, “The hardships of the road must have exhausted us. How easily we became so drunk!” Everyone laughed when they heard this.

p.src: That evening, Li Li set out wine and entertained them all, and they spent the night at his home. The next day, he again prepared food and wine for them, brought out their bundles, and returned Song Jiang and the two constables to their journey. After taking their leave, Song Jiang descended the ridge with Li Jun, Tong Wei, Tong Meng, and the two constables, and they went straight to Li Jun's home to rest. Li Jun provided food and wine and treated him with the utmost hospitality. He swore brotherhood with Song Jiang, acknowledging him as elder brother, and kept him at his home for several days. When Song Jiang insisted on leaving, Li Jun could not detain him, so he took out some silver and gave it to the two constables for their expenses. Song Jiang put the cangue on once more, gathered his bundles and baggage, bade farewell to Li Jun, Tong Meng, and Tong Wei, left the foot of Jieyang Ridge, and took the road toward Jiangzhou.

p.src: The three men had traveled for half a day, and it was already around the Hour of the Goat when they reached a place thronged with people, its streets and markets loud with commotion. As they entered the market town, they saw a crowd gathered around watching something. Song Jiang parted the crowd and squeezed through to look. It proved to be a man displaying his skill with spear and staff while selling medicinal plasters. Song Jiang and the two constables stopped and watched him perform with spear and staff for a while. The martial instructor laid down the spear and staff, then demonstrated his boxing for a time. Song Jiang cheered, "Fine work with spear, staff, fists, and feet!" The man picked up a tray and began his appeal: "I am a traveler from afar who has come to your honored town in search of a livelihood. Though I possess no astonishing skills, I rely entirely upon you generous gentlemen to support me. I have displayed what is praised abroad and demonstrated what is known nearby. If anyone needs a plaster for strained sinews, please purchase one now. If you have no need of a plaster, I beg you to grant me a little silver or a few copper coins for my traveling expenses, and not let me pass on empty-handed." The instructor passed the tray around once, but not one person gave him any money. The man said again, "Honored spectators, please be generous." He passed it around a second time. The crowd merely stared at him blankly, and again not one person offered a coin. Seeing his distress after he had gone around twice without receiving a coin, Song Jiang told one of the constables to take out five taels of silver. Song Jiang called out, "Instructor, I am a convicted man and have little to give you. Accept these five taels of silver as a small token of my regard, and do not disdain the trifling gift!" The man received the five taels of silver and held them in his palm, then put them away, saying, "In a famous place like Jieyang Town, not one discerning hero has shown his appreciation for me! Yet this generous gentleman, though presently in the custody of the authorities and merely passing through, has instead bestowed five taels of silver upon me. Just as the verse says: 'In former days men laughed at Zheng Yuanhe, who spent his wealth on songs and smiles in pleasure houses. Accustomed to generosity, he cared nothing for the riches of his house; true gallantry lies not in wearing costly clothes.' These five taels of silver are worth more than fifty from anyone else. I offer you my respects and beg to know my benefactor's honorable name, that I may proclaim it throughout the realm." Song Jiang replied, "Instructor, such a paltry thing is scarcely worth anything. There is no need to thank me." While they were speaking, a burly fellow in the crowd thrust the spectators aside, charged forward, and roared, "What damned scoundrel are you? Where did this convict come from? How dare you come here and undermine the prestige of our Jieyang Town!" Clenching both fists, he advanced to strike Song Jiang. u.src: The three men had traveled for half a day, and it was already around the Hour of the Goat when they reached a place thronged with people, its streets and markets loud with commotion.
As they entered the market town, they saw a crowd gathered around watching something.
Song Jiang parted the crowd and squeezed through to look. It proved to be a man displaying his skill with spear and staff while selling medicinal plasters.
Song Jiang and the two constables stopped and watched him perform with spear and staff for a while.
The martial instructor laid down the spear and staff, then demonstrated his boxing for a time. Song Jiang cheered, "Fine work with spear, staff, fists, and feet!"

The man picked up a tray and began his appeal: "I am a traveler from afar who has come to your honored town in search of a livelihood. Though I possess no astonishing skills, I rely entirely upon you generous gentlemen to support me. I have displayed what is praised abroad and demonstrated what is known nearby. If anyone needs a plaster for strained sinews, please purchase one now.
If you have no need of a plaster, I beg you to grant me a little silver or a few copper coins for my traveling expenses, and not let me pass on empty-handed."
The instructor passed the tray around once, but not one person gave him any money.
The man said again, "Honored spectators, please be generous."
He passed it around a second time. The crowd merely stared at him blankly, and again not one person offered a coin.
Seeing his distress after he had gone around twice without receiving a coin, Song Jiang told one of the constables to take out five taels of silver.
Song Jiang called out, "Instructor, I am a convicted man and have little to give you.
Accept these five taels of silver as a small token of my regard, and do not disdain the trifling gift!"
The man received the five taels of silver and held them in his palm, then put them away, saying, "In a famous place like Jieyang Town, not one discerning hero has shown his appreciation for me!
Yet this generous gentleman, though presently in the custody of the authorities and merely passing through, has instead bestowed five taels of silver upon me.
Just as the verse says: 'In former days men laughed at Zheng Yuanhe, who spent his wealth on songs and smiles in pleasure houses.
Accustomed to generosity, he cared nothing for the riches of his house; true gallantry lies not in wearing costly clothes.'
These five taels of silver are worth more than fifty from anyone else.
I offer you my respects and beg to know my benefactor's honorable name, that I may proclaim it throughout the realm."
Song Jiang replied, "Instructor, such a paltry thing is scarcely worth anything. There is no need to thank me."
While they were speaking, a burly fellow in the crowd thrust the spectators aside, charged forward, and roared, "What damned scoundrel are you?
Where did this convict come from?
How dare you come here and undermine the prestige of our Jieyang Town!"
Clenching both fists, he advanced to strike Song Jiang.
Had this quarrel not arisen, there would have been no occasion for several heroes, sea-churning azure dragons, to gather upon the Xunyang River;
nor for Liangshan Marsh to gain a band of heroes, fierce tigers that scale the mountains.
But why did that fellow mean to strike Song Jiang? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
